name: דְּעוּאֵל
gloss: know God, or knowledge of God; or (as Reuel, Num 2:14) friend of God
summary: A man of Gad, father of Eliasaph, the tribe’s leader in the wilderness, who brought Gad’s offering at the altar’s dedication and led its host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 10:20). The name joins אֵל “God” to the letters of “know”, as יְדִיעֲאֵל and יְדַעְיָה do: read as the plural imperative דְּעוּ, “know God”, or as a noun, “knowledge of God”. Num 2:14 names the same man רְעוּאֵל, Reuel, “friend of God”, with ר for ד; which spelling is the original the text does not settle, so the name’s tie to this root is not certain.

evidence.note: “Of Gad, Eliasaph the son of דְּעוּאֵל.”
The sixth day’s offering, by Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Gad was Eliasaph the son of דְּעוּאֵל.
The same man spelled רְעוּאֵל: “the leader of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph the son of Reuel.”
The root’s imperative sense: “let us know, let us press on to know Yahweh.”
דַּע אֶת־אֱלֹהֵי אָבִיךָ, “know the God of your father”: the imperative with God as object.

note: The Greek has Ραγουηλ in all four places (macula-lxx alignment), reading ר throughout; in the square script ד and ר are easily confused. Num 2:14 is filed under t.dl.aj (רְעוּאֵל), not under this name’s key, and is cited here only to show the alternative spelling. TIPNR’s record Deuel@Num.1.14 lists both forms.
